title: The Pure Land
hookLine: the "land of bliss" of Amitabha Buddha, a path practiced widely across East Asia

cards: The Buddha is staying in a grove near the city of Shravasti, with a great gathering of monks. He turns to his disciple Shariputra and describes a world.
Far to the west, he says, past a great many Buddha-worlds, there's a land where a Buddha lives and teaches right now. In that land, nobody suffers, in body or in mind.
The sutra goes on to fill it with jeweled trees and lotus ponds. For the coming weeks, this path stays in that land. Its name is today's word: Sukhavati.

teach.b: Back on day nine hundred ninety-two, Honen taught calling Amida's name. Now, the land that name points to. First, the name.
Sukhavati is Sanskrit, usually given in English as the land of bliss, or the happy land.

teach.h: NO PAIN OF BODY OR MIND.
teach.b: The short sutra explains it better than any dictionary: the beings there know no pain of body and no pain of mind, only causes of joy. Second, whose land it is.

The sutra says a Buddha named Amitabha lives and teaches there now. How that land came to be is a story of its own, and it starts tomorrow. Third, a detail worth keeping: the land of bliss isn't a place to retire.
In the sutra, those born there don't turn back from the path to awakening. The jeweled trees and lotus ponds aren't a reward for being finished.
They're the conditions that make the rest of the path easy: a Buddha nearby, the teaching in the air, nothing pulling anyone backward.

teach.h: A LAND BUILT FOR WAKING UP.
teach.b: A land built for waking up. Fourth, where you meet it.
In China, Japan, Korea and Vietnam, Pure Land practice lives in great temples and small home altars, at morning chanting and at the bedside of the dying.
Some Pure Land Buddhists sit in meditation too; others devote themselves to calling the Buddha's name. In Japanese the land is often called Gokuraku; in Chinese, Jile.

how: Pure Land Buddhists in China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam and beyond chant the short and long sutras on Sukhavati, call the name of Amitabha Buddha, and hope to be born in his land of bliss, where awakening is said to come without turning back.

o: the land of bliss, the Pure Land of Amitabha
a holy city in India the Buddha visited
a heaven where the finished rest forever

p: the Japanese name for the land

s: the land of bliss is a reward where beings rest forever
in the sutra, those born there keep walking the path and do not turn back.
the sutra explains the name: no pain of body or mind, only causes of joy
the Buddha gives this reason to Shariputra.
the sutra places Sukhavati far to the east
it lies far to the west, past a great many Buddha-worlds.

games.q: you're born in the land of bliss: no pain, jeweled trees, a Buddha teaching nearby. what does the sutra say comes next?
o: you rest there forever; the work is done.
you keep walking toward awakening, and you never turn back.
you're sent back to this world to start over.
games.why: the sutra says beings born there do not turn back from the path. the land is a place where waking up is made easy, not a place to stop.

practice: Call up a peaceful place you've really known, a porch, a lake, a kitchen early in the morning, and let it come in detail: the light, the sound, the air.
Then ask gently what about this place makes it easy to be kind, or clear, or awake, and stay there with your breath, letting that ease spread.

wordCard.voice: Sukhavati. The land of bliss: the Pure Land of the Buddha Amitabha, far to the west in the sutra, where beings know no pain of body or mind. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Sukhavati, the land of bliss. Japanese Gokuraku (極楽), Chinese Jile (極樂).

carryVoice: Your line: the land of bliss. Far to the west, and the path doesn't end there. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Smaller Sukhavati-vyuha (the name of the land; no turning back)
